paper_a.title: Regret Analysis of Stochastic and Nonstochastic Multi-armed Bandit Problems

paper_b.title: Exact Matrix Completion via Convex Optimization

metadata.description: Negative pair: Bubeck-Cesa-Bianchi survey on bandit regret analysis (UCB, Exp3, mirror descent, OSMD) and Candes-Recht's nuclear-norm matrix completion address fundamentally unrelated problems. Both happen to deploy generic concentration inequalities (Hoeffding/Bernstein-type) and convex-optimization vocabulary, but no theorem, definition, algorithm, problem, or proof technique on either side maps onto a counterpart on the other. The few links that exist (concentration tooling, an abstract notion of 'convex relaxation') are infrastructure rather than substantive mathematical correspondences.

matches.explanation: Both sides invoke a sub-Gaussian / Bernstein-style concentration inequality as a generic tool. In the bandit paper EP17.3 is the $\psi$-concentration $\P(\mu_i-\widehat\mu_{i,s}>\epsilon)\le e^{-s\psi^*(\epsilon)}$ used to bound UCB failure events; in the matrix completion paper LP103.13 / LP103.19 are Bernstein-type bounds on operator-valued sums that drive the dual-certificate construction. Same family of tail inequality, but neither paper cites or specialises the other; this is generic infrastructure rather than a real shared object. Low confidence because the alignment is at the level of 'both papers use concentration of measure'.

The stochastic multi-armed bandit problem (sequential decision, regret minimisation against unknown arm distributions) has no analogue in the Candes-Recht paper, which is a one-shot recovery/optimisation problem.
Adversarial bandit problem — the worst-case sequential setting against an oblivious or non-oblivious opponent has no counterpart on the matrix-completion side.
Online linear optimisation with bandit feedback — purely a sequential online-learning setting; no matrix-completion analogue.
Online combinatorial / semi-bandit problem — sequential decision over a combinatorial action set; no analogue in Candes-Recht.
Two-point feedback nonlinear adversarial bandit — gradient-style stochastic feedback; unrelated to matrix completion.
One-point feedback nonlinear adversarial bandit — no matrix-completion analogue.
Stochastic unimodal bandit on $[0,1]$ — sequential search on a one-dimensional unknown function; unrelated.
Regret and pseudo-regret functionals are bandit-specific objectives. Candes-Recht has no notion of cumulative loss against a benchmark.
Sub-Gaussian / $\psi$-moment condition on rewards. The matrix-completion paper assumes incoherence (AssumP103.1), not a moment condition on a stochastic reward, so there is no parallel hypothesis.
Two-sided strong-mode condition for SGS — geometric assumption on a unimodal function; nothing analogous in Candes-Recht.

Legendre-Fenchel transform — convex-analysis dictionary used by UCB and OMD. Candes-Recht uses convex duality (DP103.7 subgradient of nuclear norm) but never invokes Legendre conjugates explicitly, and the role here (regret control) has no parallel.
Bernoulli KL and Pinsker bound — used for the Lai-Robbins lower bound. No KL-divergence machinery appears in Candes-Recht.

Subdifferentiability, Legendre function, Bregman divergence, $\omega$-potential — convex-analysis foundations for OMD/OSMD. No counterpart in the matrix completion paper, which works with the nuclear-norm subdifferential and a tangent-space projector instead.

All 12 bandit algorithms (UCB, Exp3, Exp3.P, S-Exp3, Exp4, VE, Banditron, Exp2, OMD, OSMD, OSGD, SGS) are sequential index/weighting policies. They have no analogue in Candes-Recht, whose only algorithms are off-line SDPs (AP103.1, AP103.2). Sequential-online vs convex-program one-shot is a genuine algorithmic gap.

All 21 paper-origin upper-bound theorems concern logarithmic / $\sqrt{nK}$ regret rates of specific algorithms. None states a matrix-recovery, sample-complexity, or operator-norm result. No counterpart in Candes-Recht.

Minimax lower bound $\Omega(\sqrt{nK})$ for adversarial bandits — a sequential-game lower bound. Candes-Recht's lower bounds (OpenP103.1) discuss sample-complexity floors $nr\log n$ for matrix completion but it is an open problem rather than a theorem, and the underlying objects are different.

Auxiliary lemmas: biased gain concentration, stochastic-adversary lower-bound lemma, $\omega$-potential properties, divergence/Stokes-style identities for one-point gradient estimates, smoothed-loss lemma, SGS bracket retention. None corresponds to a matrix-completion lemma.
Bandit-specific equations: bounded-rewards UCB bound, semi-bandit and ball unbiased loss estimates, two-/one-point gradient estimates. No counterpart in Candes-Recht.

All 30 proof nodes prove regret theorems / lower bounds / lemmas specific to bandit algorithms; none aligns with a matrix-completion proof. Candes-Recht's proofs (PP103.*) drive a dual-certificate / Rudelson-style operator-norm argument that has no analogue here.
Open problem on optimal stochastic-bandit minimax-plus-distribution-dependent strategy. Distinct from Candes-Recht's open problems on sample complexity and noisy/approximate completion (OpenP103.*).
Matrix completion problem — recover an $n_1\times n_2$ matrix from a sparse subset of entries. No bandit analogue.
Rank minimisation program, NP-hard combinatorial form — no bandit counterpart.

Nuclear-norm minimisation as a convex relaxation of rank minimisation. The bandit paper relaxes via exponential weights / mirror descent, but those address sequential regret, not a static convex recovery problem; not a real match.
Generalised low-rank recovery from arbitrary linear measurements. No bandit analogue.
Nuclear norm and Schatten q-norms — matrix-norm machinery with no bandit counterpart.
Coherence of a subspace $\mu(U)$ — central matrix-completion concept; no bandit analogue.
Random orthogonal model and incoherent basis model for the underlying low-rank matrix. No bandit counterpart.
Tangent space $T$ at a low-rank matrix and its projector $\PT$ — geometric object specific to matrix manifolds. No bandit counterpart.
Sampling operator $\PO$ and Bernoulli sampling model on entries. No bandit analogue: in bandits the 'sampling' is the policy's choice of arm, fundamentally different stochastic structure.

Subgradient characterisation of the nuclear norm — used to construct dual certificates. The bandit paper uses subdifferentiability (DP17.3) of potential functions for OMD, but the role and the underlying object (matrix nuclear norm vs convex potential on a simplex) are unrelated; not an honest match.
Coherence assumptions A0/A1 on the singular vectors. No bandit analogue.

Main exact-recovery theorems: $m\gtrsim n^{6/5} r\log n$ samples suffice for nuclear-norm minimisation to recover a rank-$r$ matrix exactly. No bandit counterpart — no recovery target in the bandit setup.

Rudelson-type near-isometry $\|p^{-1}\PT\PO\PT-\PT\|\lesssim \sqrt{\mu_0 nr\log n/m}$. Operator-norm concentration on a random projection; uses the same family of probabilistic tools as the bandit concentration steps but in a completely different geometric setting.
Bernoulli deviation bound on the sampling operator $\PO$. No bandit counterpart.
Auxiliary recovery theorem in Candes-Recht; bandit paper has no parallel.

All matrix-completion lemmas (incoherent-basis spans, dual-certificate uniqueness, order-$k$ spectral bounds, Bernstein-type bounds on auxiliary operators, off-diagonal/diagonal-sandwich bounds, row-sum bounds, $\nu$-bound on $\mathcal{H}^3$). These power the dual-certificate construction; no bandit lemma performs an analogous role. Note: LP103.13 and LP103.19 are weakly tooling-aligned with EP17.3 above (already captured).
Nuclear-norm SDP and PSD trace minimisation — semidefinite programs solved off-line. The bandit paper's algorithms are sequential index/weighting policies; no algorithmic correspondence.
Sample-size threshold, power-series inversion in the operator algebra, dual-certificate ansatz $\mtx{Y}=\sum_k\PO(\PT\PO)^k\PT(\sum_j u_j v_j^*)/\dots$. All matrix-completion-specific machinery.
Open problems on optimal sample complexity, approximate-rank recovery, and noise-robust matrix completion. Disjoint from OpenP17.1 on optimal bandit strategy.

All matrix-completion proofs (uniqueness via dual certificate, Rudelson concentration, main recovery theorem, order-$k$ bounds via moment-method induction). Proof techniques (operator power series, golfing-style certificate) have no parallel in bandit regret proofs.
